newsitem.title: UK: Britain urges nationals to leave Kinshasa.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges nationals to leave Kinshasa.

text.p: Britain on Thursday urged its nationals to leave the Zairean capital Kinshasa, where there are fears of a rampage by government troops as rebel forces close in.

In a message broadcast by BBC World Service radio, the Foreign Office urged all members of the British community and Commonwealth nationals to leave the capital while commercial transport was still available.

"The situation is increasingly volatile in the Kinshasa area," the Foreign Office said. "There can be no guarantee of safety for the British community or registered Commonwealth nationals who choose to remain."
Officials said about 260 Britons and 700 Commonwealth passport holders were known to have been in Zaire, although some may have already left.
British and other allied troops are standing by in neighbouring Congo in case an evacuation of foreign nationals becomes necessary.
A rebel spokesman issued a warning on Thursday that Laurent Kabila's fighters would give Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko until Saturday to quit the capital.
